question: Which of the following countries is completely landlocked and shares an open border with India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nepal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Nepal** is a landlocked country located in South Asia. It is bordered by India to the south, east, and west, and by China (Tibet Autonomous Region) to the north.
 
• It shares an open and porous border with India, extending over **1,751 kilometers** across the states of Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, and Sikkim.
 
• Nepal is completely landlocked, meaning it does not have direct access to the sea.
 
• The Indo-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship (1950) allows citizens of both countries to travel and work across the borders without requiring a visa or passport.
 
• Nepal's strategic location in the Himalayan region makes it an important neighbor to India, both culturally and geopolitically.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Landlocked Countries:**

 
 
• A landlocked country is one that is entirely surrounded by land or has coastlines on closed seas.
 
• Nepal is one of the 44 landlocked countries in the world.
 
• Other landlocked countries in South Asia include Bhutan.
 
 
 
• **Indo-Nepal Relations:**
 
 
• India and Nepal have deep historical, cultural, religious, and economic ties.
 
• Both countries share open borders, which facilitate trade and the movement of people.
 
• India is Nepal's largest trade partner and source of foreign investment.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Significance of Nepal:**
 
 
• Nepal is home to eight of the world’s ten highest peaks, including Mount Everest, the highest point on Earth.
 
• The country lies in the Himalayan mountain range, which forms a natural barrier between the Indian subcontinent and the Tibetan Plateau.
 
 
 
• **Border Management:**
 
 
• The open border system between India and Nepal has both advantages and challenges, including issues related to security and illegal activities.
 
• Both countries are working on improving border infrastructure and security while maintaining the spirit of free movement.
